title: Uniqueness of the minimizer of the balanced optimal-transport assignment step from a balanced partition initialization
author: Wenyan Luo, Dustin G. Mixon
work: BalLOT: Balanced $k$-means clustering with optimal transport
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the article's Theorem 14 (source label 'thm.generic initialization by partition'): if the data points are generic and the initial centroids are the centroids of a balanced partition of those points, then the minimizer of the balanced optimal-transport cost over the assignment polytope is unique. The unit is above ordinary PhD qualifying level because the counted proof is a complete seventy-line research argument rather than a routine uniqueness check: it passes to distinct integral vertices of the optimal face of the assignment polytope, encodes each vertex by a set-valued assignment map of the data into the classes of the partition, shows that equality of the two costs forces a polynomial identity in the data points and hence, by genericity, an exact term-by-term cancellation, extracts from that cancellation the exchange property relating the two assignment maps on their disagreement set, and then propagates the exchange property class by class until it exhibits a strict cost decrease, contradicting optimality. Combining the geometry of the assignment polytope, genericity of the data and a combinatorial propagation of an exchange relation is research-level work in the theory of balanced clustering and optimal transport, well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
